my-father--le-bijou-1922.description: Le Bijou, “the jewel”, is José “Pepín” García's tribute to his father, born in 1922. A Nicaraguan puro under a near-black Habano Oscuro wrapper, it is full-bodied and markedly aromatic, with pepper and earth over a core of espresso and dark chocolate.

thirds.notes: Pepper and earth lead, with dark chocolate and espresso underneath.
The pepper eases for creamier, slightly sweeter coffee and nutty notes.
Coffee concentrates over cocoa and earth, and the pepper returns toward a woody finish.

sources.title: halfwheel – Le Bijou 1922 Robusto review
The Cigar Authority – Le Bijou 1922 (My Father description)

my-father--my-father.description: The original My Father, released in 2008, was blended by Jaime García as a tribute to his father, José “Pepín” García. Aged Nicaraguan long filler from the family's own farms sits under a Nicaraguan Habano rosado wrapper; full in strength, it offers cedar, nuts and black pepper with cinnamon, nutmeg, leather and cocoa.

sources.title: Holt's – My Father brand page (line descriptions)

my-father--connecticut.description: Blended by Pepín and Jaime García at their Estelí factory, the My Father Connecticut pairs a smooth Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler, including an aromatic leaf given a special fermentation. Creamy and nutty on top, with spice and earth underneath, it is fuller than most Connecticut-wrapped cigars.

sources.title: Holt's – My Father brand page (line descriptions)
Blind Man's Puff – My Father Connecticut Corona Gorda blind review

thirds.notes: Pepper and spice lead over leather and a nutty note, and the flavours settle into better balance by the end of the third.
Cedar and coffee-like tobacco with peppery nutmeg, then earth and green pepper as the body fills out.
Pepper and cedar remain with light nutmeg, fresh grass and hay, and a faint floral sweetness.

my-father--the-judge.description: The Judge is a box-pressed Nicaraguan blend from the García family, with a cinnamon-hued Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over long filler from Estelí, Jalapa and Namanjí. Full in strength, it shows leather, cedar, earth and pepper with the house spice, and closes on a toasty, nutty finish.

sources.title: Holt's – My Father brand page (line descriptions)
Cigar World – Member review My Father The Judge

thirds.notes: A red-pepper start with dark chocolate, leather, dark-roast espresso and Spanish cedar.
Chocolate, leather and pepper merge, joined by caramel and toast, at the same steady strength.
Dark chocolate on toasted rye, cedar, nutmeg and strong red pepper over a creamy texture, as the nicotine rises markedly.

my-father--la-opulencia.description: La Opulencia combines a dark San Andrés oscuro wrapper from Mexico with Nicaraguan binder and filler, made by the García family in Estelí. Hearty and full, it brings cocoa, cinnamon and spice with wood, black pepper and espresso, all on a leathery texture.

Cigar Obsession – My Father La Opulencia Toro Gordo review

thirds.notes: Dry, dark cocoa with espresso and black pepper, and an aged-tobacco sweetness; the smoke is light and airy at first.
Pepper becomes the dominant note and coats the palate, with rich tobacco, cocoa and a hint of cedar and a longer, spicier finish.
Cocoa and espresso deepen with caramel, leather, toasted wood and earth, while pepper and spice stay bold on the retrohale.

my-father--la-gran-oferta.description: La Gran Oferta revives the name of an old cigar brand, with boxes and bands in period artwork. Made at the My Father factory, it covers all-Nicaraguan binder and filler with an oily Cuban-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador; medium to full, it offers wood, leather and molasses-like sweetness with balanced spice.

thirds.notes: Black pepper and spice over dry earth at first, settling into butter, a plum-like note and gentle sweetness.
Earth and wood carry the middle, with milk chocolate, coffee and cream, and spice that keeps returning.
Strength and spice pick up toward the end, with red pepper, charred oak, sweet cream, hay and peanut.

my-father--la-promesa.description: La Promesa, “the promise”, honours a pledge Pepín García made to his family when he left Cuba in the early 2000s. A Cuban-seed Habano wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler in a medium-to-full blend that is nutty and woody, with a bright, zesty edge.

thirds.notes: Caramel, milk chocolate and nuts, or earth with baker's chocolate, over black and white pepper.
Baking spice and dark fruit come forward, nuts and white pepper continue, and a creamy cedar note arrives around the midpoint.
Dark fruit, baking spice and oak with white pepper, as earth grows and a slight bitterness appears at the close.

my-father--blue.description: Blue was the first blend from the García family's Honduran factory, made with tobacco from their Finca La Opulencia in Talanga. Honduran long filler from Corojo and Criollo seeds sits under a Connecticut broadleaf rosado wrapper; medium to full, it offers leather, cayenne-like heat, wood, sweetness and dried fruit. The blue and white dress honours the Honduran flag.

thirds.notes: Leather leads with black pepper and a delicate floral touch, alongside citrus peel, brown sugar, light cinnamon and black coffee.
The smoke turns thicker and creamier, leather deepens, cedar and a savoury note appear, and the citrus and coffee carry on.
Bolder, with leather and cedar, cinnamon, some earth and more pepper, as the body reaches medium to full.

my-father--la-lealtad.description: La Lealtad, “loyalty”, is the García family's second Honduran cigar after Blue, made with tobacco from their Finca La Opulencia in Talanga. An Ecuadorian rosado oscuro wrapper covers aged Nicaraguan and Honduran long filler; medium to full, it carries coffee bean, cocoa, leather, red pepper and nutmeg over earth, with a hint of raisin.

thirds.notes: Apricot with a citrus edge, brown sugar and light nougat, then strong black coffee, a little earth and leather and lingering black pepper.
Earth and black coffee grow while the sweet notes recede, and the finish stays coffee-led with pepper.
Apricot and brown sugar return, earth eases and the coffee softens, closing on fruit and black pepper.
